Which statement is correct about a credit note?
A It is sent by Amber when Bashir buys goods.
B It is sent by Amber when Bashir returns goods.
C It is sent by Bashir when he buys goods.
D It is sent by Bashir when he returns goods.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Jack’s bank statement showed a credit balance of $600 on 30 June. It contained bank
charges, $20, which did not appear in the cash book. Cheques, $150, issued by Jack did not
appear on the bank statement.
Which value for bank appeared in Jack’s statement of financial position on 30 June?
A $450 current asset
B $580 current asset
C $620 current liability
D $750 current liability

parts.label: (f)
parts.text:
A retailer has an item of inventory which cost $60 and which is on sale at $50.
How does the retailer value this item in his statement of financial position?
A at cost price, to allow for losses as early as possible
B at cost price, to avoid recognising profit before it is earned
C at selling price, to allow for losses as early as possible
D at selling price, to avoid recognising profit before it is earned

parts.label: (g)
parts.text:
A statement of financial position showed non-current assets, current assets, current liabilities
and non-current liabilities.
What equals owner’s capital?
A current assets – current liabilities
B non-current assets
C total assets – current liabilities
D total assets – total liabilities

parts.label: (h)
parts.text:
Which statement is true about dividends paid on ordinary shares?
A They appear in the appropriation account and are paid to partners.
B They appear in the income statement and are paid to partners.
C They appear in the statement of changes in equity and are paid
to members of a company.
D They appear in the statement of financial position and are paid
to members of a company.

that period his sales were $1200. He paid $820 to suppliers and a supplier’s invoice for $70
was unpaid. His cost of sales was $800.
What was the cost of the inventory which was destroyed?
A $50
B $90
C $310
D $380

text: Amina and Doreen formed a partnership on 1 January 2016, buying and selling calculators. On
that date they each paid $5000 into the business bank account.
Amina also brought in a delivery vehicle valued at $8100 to the partnership and Doreen brought in
fixtures and fittings valued at $4800.
The partnership agreement stated that profits and losses would be shared in the ratio 2:1.
Depreciation was to be provided on a monthly basis, at the rate of 20% per annum for the delivery
vehicle and 10% per annum for the fixtures and fittings.
In the first month of trading they had the following transactions.
Jan 1 Paid 3 months’ rent totalling $2700, by cheque
2 Bought 1000 calculators for $4 each from Bertie on credit
6 Sold 800 calculators for cash for $10 each, keeping $100 in hand and banking the
remaining cash
13 Sold 50 calculators for $10 each to Charlie on credit
20 Paid Bertie by cheque, deducting 3% discount for prompt payment
31 Paid wages for the month, $800, by credit transfer
REQUIRED
